---- MODULE W4Od16m1p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Stations, MaxSlot, RxIds

VARIABLES holder, cap, dispenseLog, waiting

vars == <<holder, cap, dispenseLog, waiting>>

N == Cardinality(Stations)

StationOrder == CHOOSE seq \in [1..N -> Stations] :
                    \A a \in Stations : \E i \in 1..N : seq[i] = a

NextStation(a) ==
    LET i == CHOOSE k \in 1..N : StationOrder[k] = a
    IN StationOrder[(i % N) + 1]

FilledSlots == { dispenseLog[i].slot : i \in DOMAIN dispenseLog }

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Stations
    /\ cap \in 1..MaxSlot
    /\ dispenseLog \in Seq([slot: 1..MaxSlot, by: Stations])
    /\ waiting \in SUBSET RxIds

Init ==
    /\ holder = StationOrder[1]
    /\ cap = 1
    /\ dispenseLog = << >>
    /\ waiting = {}

PassToken ==
    /\ holder' = NextStation(holder)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, dispenseLog, waiting>>

AddCapacity ==
    /\ cap < MaxSlot
    /\ cap' = cap + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, dispenseLog, waiting>>

DropCapacity ==
    /\ cap > 1
    /\ cap \notin FilledSlots
    /\ cap' = cap - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, dispenseLog, waiting>>

Prescribe ==
    /\ \E r \in RxIds \ waiting :
        /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {r}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cap, dispenseLog>>

Dispense ==
    /\ \E r \in waiting, s \in 1..cap :
        /\ s \notin FilledSlots
        /\ dispenseLog' = Append(dispenseLog, [slot |-> s, by |-> holder])
        /\ waiting' = waiting \ {r}
        /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, cap>>

Next ==
    \/ PassToken
    \/ AddCapacity
    \/ DropCapacity
    \/ Prescribe
    \/ Dispense

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleDispense ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN dispenseLog :
        (i # j) => dispenseLog[i].slot # dispenseLog[j].slot
====
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser is organized as a ring of dispensing
stations that pass a single physical token around the ring; only the
station currently holding the token may fill a prescription into a
numbered dispensing slot. Slots are numbered 1..MaxSlot, but the number
of slots that are actually online (the capacity) changes at runtime as
drawers are brought in service or taken out for cleaning. New
prescriptions arrive and sit in a waiting pool until some token-holding
station fills one. Filling a prescription writes an append-only dispense
log entry recording which slot was used and which station did it; a slot
that has already been filled can never be reused for another
prescription. The capacity may grow (bringing a fresh drawer online) up
to MaxSlot, and may shrink (taking the highest-numbered drawer offline)
only when that top slot has never been filled.

The system model has these actions: PassToken (advance the token to the
next station in the ring), AddCapacity (bring one more slot online),
DropCapacity (take the top slot offline when it was never filled),
Prescribe (a new prescription arrives into the waiting pool), and
Dispense (the token holder fills a waiting prescription into a free,
online, never-before-used slot).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No dispensing slot is ever allocated to two different
prescriptions, i.e. no slot number appears twice in the append-only
dispense log.

---- MODULE W4Od1m2p0t0 ----
EXTENDS FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Aircraft, Sensors, NoReq

VARIABLES phase, requester, ballots, holds, crashed

vars == <<phase, requester, ballots, holds, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ requester = NoReq
    /\ ballots = [s \in Sensors |-> "abstain"]
    /\ holds = [a \in Aircraft |-> FALSE]
    /\ crashed = {}

BeginRequest ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ \E a \in Aircraft :
        /\ phase' = "voting"
        /\ requester' = a
        /\ ballots' = [s \in Sensors |-> "abstain"]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<holds, crashed>>

CastYes ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E s \in Sensors \ crashed :
        /\ ballots[s] = "abstain"
        /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![s] = "yes"]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, requester, holds, crashed>>

CastNo ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E s \in Sensors \ crashed :
        /\ ballots[s] = "abstain"
        /\ ballots' = [ballots EXCEPT ![s] = "no"]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, requester, holds, crashed>>

CrashSensor ==
    /\ \E s \in Sensors \ crashed :
        crashed' = crashed \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, requester, ballots, holds>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A s \in Sensors : ballots[s] = "yes"
    /\ \A a \in Aircraft : ~holds[a]
    /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![requester] = TRUE]
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ requester' = NoReq
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballots, crashed>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ ~(\A s \in Sensors : ballots[s] = "yes")
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ requester' = NoReq
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballots, holds, crashed>>

Release ==
    /\ \E a \in Aircraft :
        /\ holds[a]
        /\ holds' = [holds EXCEPT ![a] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, requester, ballots, crashed>>

Next ==
    \/ BeginRequest
    \/ CastYes
    \/ CastNo
    \/ CrashSensor
    \/ Commit
    \/ Abort
    \/ Release

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RunwayMutex ==
    \A a, b \in Aircraft : (holds[a] /\ holds[b]) => (a = b)
====
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator grants exclusive use of a single runway
to aircraft using a two-phase-commit handshake. A coordinator opens a
transaction on behalf of one requesting aircraft and asks every runway
sensor to vote on whether the runway is clear. Each sensor casts a yes
or no ballot. The grant is committed only if every sensor voted yes and
no aircraft currently holds the runway; otherwise the transaction is
aborted. Any sensor may crash silently: once crashed it never casts a
ballot again, so its ballot stays abstaining and the transaction can
never reach unanimous yes, which safely blocks the commit rather than
granting on incomplete information. An aircraft holding the runway may
release it.

The system model has these actions: BeginRequest (open a transaction for
some aircraft and reset all ballots to abstain), CastYes and CastNo (a
non-crashed sensor votes), CrashSensor (a sensor crashes silently),
Commit (grant the runway to the requester only when all sensors voted
yes and no aircraft holds it), Abort (the coordinator times
out and cancels the transaction whenever the sensors have not all voted
yes, which also covers the case where a crashed sensor leaves a ballot
abstaining forever), and Release (a holder gives up the runway).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one aircraft ever holds the runway at the same
time, so no two distinct aircraft can both be in the holding state.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Robots, Pallets, Idle

VARIABLES version, snapshot, target, shipLog, crashed

vars == <<version, snapshot, target, shipLog, crashed>>

Shipped == { shipLog[i] : i \in DOMAIN shipLog }

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ snapshot = [r \in Robots |-> -1]
    /\ target = [r \in Robots |-> Idle]
    /\ shipLog = << >>
    /\ crashed = {}

Read(r) ==
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ target[r] = Idle
    /\ \E p \in Pallets \ Shipped :
        /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![r] = version]
        /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, shipLog, crashed>>

Ship(r) ==
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ target[r] # Idle
    /\ snapshot[r] = version
    /\ target[r] \notin Shipped
    /\ shipLog' = Append(shipLog, target[r])
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![r] = -1]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

RetryStale(r) ==
    /\ target[r] # Idle
    /\ snapshot[r] # version
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![r] = -1]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, shipLog, crashed>>

Crash(r) ==
    /\ r \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {r}
    /\ snapshot' = [snapshot EXCEPT ![r] = -1]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![r] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, shipLog>>

Recover(r) ==
    /\ r \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, snapshot, target, shipLog>>

Next ==
    \E r \in Robots :
        \/ Read(r)
        \/ Ship(r)
        \/ RetryStale(r)
        \/ Crash(r)
        \/ Recover(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ShipOnce ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN shipLog : (i # j) => shipLog[i] # shipLog[j]
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet ships pallets out of a shared staging area using
optimistic locking with retry. There is one shared version counter. When
a robot wants to ship a pallet it first reads the current version into
its private snapshot and picks a not-yet-shipped pallet as its target.
To actually ship, the robot re-checks that the version has not changed
since its snapshot (an optimistic compare); only then does it perform the
irreversible shipment, append the pallet to the append-only ship log, and
bump the shared version. If the version moved on under it, the robot's
snapshot is stale, so it abandons the attempt and retries. Any robot may
crash silently at any time, dropping whatever attempt it had in flight;
a crashed robot can later recover and rejoin the fleet.

The system model has these actions: Read (an idle robot snapshots the
version and claims a target pallet), Ship (a robot with a fresh snapshot
irreversibly ships its target and bumps the version), RetryStale (a robot
whose snapshot no longer matches the version drops its attempt), Crash (a
robot fails silently and loses its in-flight attempt), and Recover (a
crashed robot rejoins).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No pallet is ever shipped more than once, i.e. no pallet
appears twice in the append-only ship log.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Instances, Pallets, MaxVer, NoP

VARIABLES remaining, ver, snap, claim, finalized

vars == <<remaining, ver, snap, claim, finalized>>

Bump(n) == (n + 1) % (MaxVer + 1)

Init ==
    /\ remaining = Pallets
    /\ ver = [p \in Pallets |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ claim = [i \in Instances |-> NoP]
    /\ finalized = << >>

Acquire(i) ==
    /\ claim[i] = NoP
    /\ \E p \in remaining :
        /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![i] = ver[p]]
        /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![i] = p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, ver, finalized>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ claim[i] # NoP
    /\ claim[i] \in remaining
    /\ snap[i] = ver[claim[i]]
    /\ finalized' = Append(finalized, claim[i])
    /\ remaining' = remaining \ {claim[i]}
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![claim[i]] = Bump(@)]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![i] = NoP]
    /\ UNCHANGED snap

Abort(i) ==
    /\ claim[i] # NoP
    /\ (claim[i] \notin remaining \/ snap[i] # ver[claim[i]])
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![i] = NoP]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, ver, snap, finalized>>

Interfere(p) ==
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![p] = Bump(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<remaining, snap, claim, finalized>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Acquire(i) \/ Commit(i) \/ Abort(i)
    \/ \E p \in Pallets : Interfere(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FinalizeOnce ==
    \A a, b \in DOMAIN finalized : (a # b) => finalized[a] # finalized[b]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Instances = {x, y}
    Pallets = {q1, q2, q3}
    MaxVer = 1
    NoP = NoP
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT FinalizeOnce
nl:
Two independent warehouse robot fleets (two instances) draw from one
shared pool of pallets and finalize shipments using optimistic locking
with retry. Every pallet carries its own version number. When an instance
wants to finalize a pallet it acquires a claim: it reads that pallet's
current version into its private snapshot and remembers the pallet. To
finalize, the instance re-checks that the pallet is still in the shared
pool and that its snapshot still equals the pallet's version; only then
does it perform the irreversible finalize, record the pallet in the
append-only finalized log, remove the pallet from the shared pool, and
bump that pallet's version. If the pallet was taken by the other instance
or its version moved, the snapshot is stale and the instance aborts and
may retry. Concurrent activity by either instance can interfere with a
pallet's version at any time, which is what makes optimistic snapshots go
stale.

The system model has these actions: Acquire (an idle instance snapshots a
pooled pallet's version and claims it), Commit (an instance with a valid
snapshot irreversibly finalizes its claimed pallet, logs it, removes it
from the pool, and bumps its version), Abort (an instance drops a claim
whose pallet left the pool or whose snapshot went stale), and Interfere
(concurrent activity bumps a pallet's version).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No pallet is ever finalized more than once, i.e. no
pallet appears twice in the append-only finalized log.

---- MODULE W4Od2m5p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, Updates, Quorum

VARIABLES votes, applied, acked, slow

vars == <<votes, applied, acked, slow>>

Init ==
    /\ votes = [u \in Updates |-> {}]
    /\ applied = {}
    /\ acked = {}
    /\ slow = {}

Vote(n, u) ==
    /\ n \notin slow
    /\ n \notin votes[u]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![u] = @ \cup {n}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<applied, acked, slow>>

BecomeSlow(n) ==
    /\ n \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, applied, acked>>

SpeedUp(n) ==
    /\ n \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, applied, acked>>

Commit(u) ==
    /\ u \notin applied
    /\ Cardinality(votes[u]) >= Quorum
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, acked, slow>>

Ack(u) ==
    /\ u \in applied
    /\ u \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, applied, slow>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes, u \in Updates : Vote(n, u)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : BecomeSlow(n) \/ SpeedUp(n)
    \/ \E u \in Updates : Commit(u) \/ Ack(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    acked \subseteq applied
====
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet maintains a shared inventory record that is
replicated across several nodes. Every update to the record must be
ratified by a quorum of nodes before it is applied, and only after it is
applied may it be acknowledged back to the robot that proposed it. Each
node votes at most once per update. A node may be slow but never fails:
while it is slow it cannot cast votes, but it can always speed back up
and resume voting, so no update is permanently stuck as long as a quorum
eventually forms. An update is committed (applied to the record) once a
quorum of nodes has voted for it; acknowledging an update to the client
is only allowed once that update has actually been applied, which is what
prevents an acknowledged update from being silently lost.

The system model has these actions: Vote (a non-slow node ratifies an
update), BecomeSlow (a node becomes temporarily slow and stops voting),
SpeedUp (a slow node recovers and can vote again), Commit (apply an update
whose votes have reached the quorum), and Ack (acknowledge an
already-applied update to the client).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every update that has been acknowledged to a robot has
actually been applied to the shared record, so no acknowledged update is
ever lost.

---- MODULE W4Od4m7p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

CONSTANTS Bays, NoOwner, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES reg, cached, lastAdvancer, crashed

vars == <<reg, cached, lastAdvancer, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ reg = [owner |-> NoOwner, epoch |-> 0]
    /\ cached = [b \in Bays |-> -1]
    /\ lastAdvancer = NoOwner
    /\ crashed = {}

Acquire(b) ==
    /\ b \notin crashed
    /\ reg.epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ reg' = [owner |-> b, epoch |-> reg.epoch + 1]
    /\ cached' = [cached EXCEPT ![b] = reg.epoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lastAdvancer, crashed>>

Advance(b) ==
    /\ b \notin crashed
    /\ reg.owner = b
    /\ cached[b] = reg.epoch
    /\ lastAdvancer' = b
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, cached, crashed>>

Revoke ==
    /\ reg.owner # NoOwner
    /\ reg.epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ reg' = [owner |-> NoOwner, epoch |-> reg.epoch + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cached, lastAdvancer, crashed>>

Crash(b) ==
    /\ b \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, cached, lastAdvancer>>

Recover(b) ==
    /\ b \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, cached, lastAdvancer>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Acquire(b) \/ Advance(b) \/ Crash(b) \/ Recover(b)
    \/ Revoke

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyCurrentOwnerIsFresh ==
    \A b \in Bays : (cached[b] = reg.epoch) => (reg.owner = b)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bays = {b1, b2, b3}
    NoOwner = NoOwner
    MaxEpoch = 3
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyCurrentOwnerIsFresh
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line is controlled through a single compare-and-swap
authority register. The register names the bay that currently owns the
right to advance the conveyor together with an epoch number; every time
ownership changes the epoch is bumped. When a bay acquires the register
it becomes the owner and caches the new epoch locally. A bay may advance
the conveyor (perform an action) only when it is the register's current
owner and its cached epoch still equals the register's epoch, so a bay
whose ownership was revoked or superseded holds a stale cached epoch and
is locked out. Ownership can be revoked, which bumps the epoch and clears
the owner, immediately staling whoever held it. Any bay may crash
silently and stop participating, and a crashed bay may later recover.

The system model has these actions: Acquire (a bay compare-and-swaps
itself in as owner and caches the fresh epoch), Advance (the current,
non-stale owner performs a conveyor action and records it), Revoke (clear
the owner and bump the epoch, staling the old owner), Crash (a bay fails
silently), and Recover (a crashed bay returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A bay's cached epoch equals the register's current epoch
only when that bay is the register's current owner, so no stale or
non-owning bay can ever pass the authorization check to act.

---- MODULE W4Od12m3p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Replicas, Units, Majority, MaxTerm, NoLeader

VARIABLES term, leader, support, issued, down

vars == <<term, leader, support, issued, down>>

IssuedSet == { issued[i] : i \in DOMAIN issued }

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ support = {}
    /\ issued = << >>
    /\ down = {}

StartElection ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ support' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, down>>

CastVote(r) ==
    /\ r \notin down
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ r \notin support
    /\ support' = support \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, issued, down>>

TakeLeadership(c) ==
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ Cardinality(support) >= Majority
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, support, issued, down>>

IssueUnit(u) ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ leader \notin down
    /\ u \notin IssuedSet
    /\ issued' = Append(issued, u)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, support, down>>

Fail(r) ==
    /\ r \notin down
    /\ down' = down \cup {r}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = r THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, support, issued>>

Restore(r) ==
    /\ r \in down
    /\ down' = down \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, support, issued>>

Next ==
    \/ StartElection
    \/ \E r \in Replicas : CastVote(r) \/ TakeLeadership(r) \/ Fail(r) \/ Restore(r)
    \/ \E u \in Units : IssueUnit(u)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

IssueAtMostOnce ==
    \A i, j \in DOMAIN issued : (i # j) => issued[i] # issued[j]
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Replicas = {s1, s2, s3}
    Units = {u1, u2}
    Majority = 2
    MaxTerm = 3
    NoLeader = NoLeader
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT IssueAtMostOnce
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker is replicated for high availability and
uses leader election with failover to decide which replica is allowed to
irreversibly issue blood units. Elections proceed in terms: starting a
new election bumps the term, clears the current leader, and resets the
tally of supporting votes. A live replica casts a vote while no leader is
established; once a candidate has gathered a majority of votes it takes
leadership. Only the standing, non-failed leader may issue a blood unit,
and a given unit can be issued only if it has never been issued before,
recording it in the append-only issue log. Any replica may fail silently;
if the failed replica was the leader, leadership is vacated and a fresh
election with failover can select a new leader. A failed replica may be
restored.

The system model has these actions: StartElection (bump the term and
reset votes), CastVote (a live replica supports the current election),
TakeLeadership (a candidate with a majority becomes leader), IssueUnit
(the live leader irreversibly issues a never-before-issued unit), Fail (a
replica fails silently, vacating leadership if it held it), and Restore (a
failed replica returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No blood unit is ever issued more than once, i.e. no
unit appears twice in the append-only issue log.

---- MODULE W4Od16m6p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Holders, Capacity, MaxTime, LeaseDur

VARIABLES clock, held, expiry, crashed

vars == <<clock, held, expiry, crashed>>

Init ==
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ held = {}
    /\ expiry = [h \in Holders |-> -1]
    /\ crashed = {}

Tick ==
    /\ clock < MaxTime
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, expiry, crashed>>

Grant(h) ==
    /\ h \notin held
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(held) < Capacity
    /\ held' = held \cup {h}
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![h] = clock + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, crashed>>

Renew(h) ==
    /\ h \in held
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![h] = clock + LeaseDur]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, held, crashed>>

Expire(h) ==
    /\ h \in held
    /\ expiry[h] <= clock
    /\ held' = held \ {h}
    /\ expiry' = [expiry EXCEPT ![h] = -1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, crashed>>

Crash(h) ==
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, held, expiry>>

Recover(h) ==
    /\ h \in crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, held, expiry>>

Next ==
    \/ Tick
    \/ \E h \in Holders : Grant(h) \/ Renew(h) \/ Expire(h) \/ Crash(h) \/ Recover(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapacityRespected ==
    Cardinality(held) <= Capacity
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Holders = {h1, h2, h3}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxTime = 2
    LeaseDur = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser hands out a bounded number of
concurrent dispensing leases: at most Capacity leases may be active at
once. Ownership is lease-based with expiry. A global clock ticks forward.
When a holder is granted a lease it joins the set of active holders and
its lease is stamped with an expiry deadline LeaseDur ticks in the
future; a grant is only permitted while the number of currently active
holders is below the capacity. A holder may renew its lease, pushing the
deadline further out. Once the clock reaches a lease's deadline the lease
expires and the holder is dropped, freeing capacity. A holder may crash
silently; crucially a crashed holder does not release its lease
immediately, but its lease still expires on schedule, so the capacity
self-heals. A crashed holder may recover.

The system model has these actions: Tick (advance the clock), Grant (give
a lease to a new holder only while below capacity), Renew (extend a
holder's deadline), Expire (drop a holder whose deadline has passed),
Crash (a holder fails silently while still holding its lease), and Recover
(a crashed holder returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of holders with an active dispensing lease
never exceeds the configured capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od15m3p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxTerm, MaxCap, NoLeader

VARIABLES term, leader, running, matchCap, down

vars == <<term, leader, running, matchCap, down>>

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ running = {}
    /\ matchCap = 1
    /\ down = {}

Elect(c) ==
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<running, matchCap, down>>

EnterAuction(c) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ running = {}
    /\ running' = {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, matchCap, down>>

LeaveAuction(c) ==
    /\ c \in running
    /\ running' = running \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, matchCap, down>>

RaiseCap ==
    /\ matchCap < MaxCap
    /\ matchCap' = matchCap + 1

CONSTANTS

nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction is run by a cluster of matching nodes
that use leader election with failover to decide which single node is
allowed to run the auction's critical matching section against the shared
order book. Elections proceed in terms; electing a node bumps the term
and installs it as leader. Only the current leader may enter the critical
matching section, and only when the section is currently empty, which is
what enforces exclusive access. A node in the section may leave it. The
auction's matching capacity (how many orders it will cross this round)
changes at runtime and can be raised or lowered independently of who is
matching. Any node may fail; failing vacates leadership if it was the
leader and ejects the node from the matching section, letting a failover
election pick a new leader. A failed node may be restored.

The system model has these actions: Elect (bump the term and install a
leader), EnterAuction (the leader enters the empty matching section),
LeaveAuction (a node leaves the section), RaiseCap and LowerCap (the
matching capacity changes at runtime), Fail (a node fails, vacating
leadership and leaving the section), and Restore (a failed node returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one node is ever inside the critical matching
section at a time, so two distinct nodes never run the auction against the
order book simultaneously.

A bank's interbank settlement batch moves money among a shared set of
accounts. Two independent settlement engines run over the same shared
pool of accounts, and each engine independently runs leader election with
failover to decide which node currently drives it. Every unit of money is
either resting in an account or briefly in flight during a settlement
step; the grand total of money in the system never changes, because money
is only ever moved, never minted or burned. A live leader of either
engine may withdraw a unit from an account (placing it in flight) or
settle an in-flight unit into an account. Because both engines share the
one pool of accounts and the one in-flight reserve, their steps interleave

and triggering failover; a failed node may be restored.

installs a leader), Withdraw (a leader removes a unit from an account into

and Restore (a failed node returns).

currently in flight always equals the fixed system total, so no money is
ever created or destroyed.

nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags onto a shared sorting belt that has
a strict bounded capacity. Two independent router instances share the one
belt and the one arrival queue as a common pool. The system uses
epoch-numbered reconfiguration: a reconfiguration bumps the global epoch,
which leaves every router's cached epoch stale until it re-syncs. A router
may only move bags while its cached epoch equals the current global epoch;
a stale router must sync first. Bags arrive into the shared queue. A
current-epoch router may load a queued bag onto the belt, but only while
the belt is below its capacity, and may unload a bag off the belt. Because
both router instances draw from the same queue and push onto the same
belt, their loads and unloads interleave, yet the belt must never hold
more than its capacity.

The system model has these actions: Reconfigure (bump the global epoch,
staling all routers), Sync (a stale router catches up to the current
epoch), Arrive (a bag joins the shared queue), Load (a current-epoch
router moves a queued bag onto the belt while below capacity), and Unload
(a current-epoch router removes a bag from the belt).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of bags on the sorting belt never exceeds the
belt's configured capacity.

An elevator bank in a skyscraper owns a fixed fleet of elevator cars. A
dispatcher hands cars out to demand zones using lease-based ownership with
expiry: a leased car serves a zone until its lease deadline passes, then
returns to the central depot. A global clock ticks forward. Every car is
always either idle in the depot or leased to exactly one zone, and the
total number of cars never changes -- cars are only ever moved between the
depot and zones, never built or scrapped. Leasing a car takes it from the
depot and stamps the zone's lease with a deadline; a zone may renew its
lease to push the deadline out; when the deadline passes a car returns
from the zone to the depot. A privileged admin override may reassign a car
from one zone directly to another, bypassing the depot and the lease
timing.

a depot car to a zone and stamp its deadline), Renew (extend a zone's
lease deadline), Expire (return a car from a zone to the depot once its
deadline has passed), and AdminReassign (the admin override moves a car
from one zone directly to another).

leased out across all zones always equals the fixed fleet size, so no
elevator car is ever created or destroyed.

nl:
A warehouse robot fleet coordinates exclusive access to a shared aisle
using a token ring: exactly one robot holds the ring's token, and only the
current token holder is authorized to perform work on the aisle. The ring
membership changes at runtime -- its capacity grows as new robots are
admitted and shrinks as robots leave -- so a robot that has left the ring
is no longer authorized and any belief it still holds the token is stale.
A robot outside the ring may request to join, and a pending robot may be
admitted into the ring. The token may be passed to any other current ring
member. The holder may perform a unit of work only while it is genuinely a
current member of the ring. A member other than the current holder may
leave the ring; the holder itself cannot leave while holding the token, so
the token is never stranded on a departed, unauthorized robot.

The system model has these actions: RequestJoin (an outside robot asks to
join), Admit (a pending robot enters the ring, growing capacity),
PassToken (the token moves to another ring member), Act (the holder
performs a unit of work while it is a current member), and Leave (a
non-holder member departs the ring, shrinking capacity).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The robot holding the token is always a current member of
the ring, so no departed, stale, or otherwise unauthorized robot can ever
hold the token and act.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p6t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Coordinators, Cranes, MaxMoves

VARIABLES phase, prepared, cleared, moves

vars == <<phase, prepared, cleared, moves>>

Init ==
    /\ phase = [i \in Coordinators |-> "idle"]
    /\ prepared = [i \in Coordinators |-> {}]
    /\ cleared = [i \in Coordinators |-> {}]
    /\ moves = 0

Begin(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] \in {"idle", "done"}
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "voting"]
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED moves

Prepare(i, c) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ c \notin prepared[i]
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![i] = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cleared, moves>>

Commit(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "done"]
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![i] = prepared[i]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<prepared, moves>>

Abort(i) ==
    /\ phase[i] = "voting"
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![i] = "idle"]
    /\ prepared' = [prepared EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![i] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED moves

Move(i, c) ==
    /\ c \in cleared[i]
    /\ moves < MaxMoves
    /\ moves' = moves + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, prepared, cleared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Coordinators : Begin(i) \/ Commit(i) \/ Abort(i)
    \/ \E i \in Coordinators, c \in Cranes : Prepare(i, c) \/ Move(i, c)

    \A i \in Coordinators : cleared[i] \subseteq prepared[i]
====
nl:
A container-ship crane yard coordinates crane moves through two-phase
commit. Two independent coordinators run over the shared pool of cranes;
each coordinator drives its own transaction. A transaction begins by
opening a voting phase and clearing any prior state. During voting, cranes
prepare (vote yes) for that coordinator's transaction. If the coordinator
commits, exactly the cranes that prepared in this transaction become the
cleared set that is authorized to perform physical moves; if it aborts, no
crane is authorized. Beginning a new transaction wipes the previous
cleared set, so a crane authorized in an earlier committed transaction
becomes stale and is no longer allowed to move. A crane may perform a
physical move only while it is in its coordinator's current cleared set,
which keeps unauthorized cranes (never prepared) and stale cranes
(authorized in a past round) from acting.

The system model has these actions: Begin (open a fresh voting phase and
clear prior state), Prepare (a crane votes yes in the current
transaction), Commit (authorize exactly the cranes that prepared this
round), Abort (end the transaction authorizing nobody), and Move (a
currently-cleared crane performs a physical move).

SAFETY PROPERTY: For each coordinator, every crane authorized to move
(in the cleared set) actually prepared in the current transaction, so no
unauthorized or stale crane is ever cleared to act.

VARIABLES epoch, unwaxed, waxLog, stationEpoch, slow

Sync(s) ==

    /\ stationEpoch[s] < epoch
    /\ stationEpoch' = [stationEpoch EXCEPT ![s] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, unwaxed, waxLog, slow>>

BecomeSlow(s) ==
    /\ s \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, unwaxed, waxLog, stationEpoch>>

SpeedUp(s) ==
    /\ s \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, unwaxed, waxLog, stationEpoch>>

Wax(s, car) ==
    /\ s \notin slow
    /\ stationEpoch[s] = epoch
    /\ car \in unwaxed
    /\ waxLog' = Append(waxLog, car)
    /\ unwaxed' = unwaxed \ {car}

    \/ \E s \in Stations : Sync(s) \/ BecomeSlow(s) \/ SpeedUp(s)

    \A car \in Cars : (car \in WaxedSet) => (car \notin unwaxed)

nl:
A car-wash conveyor line applies a final wax coat to each car -- an
irreversible finishing step that must be applied to any given car at most
once. The line uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration: reconfiguring the line
bumps the global epoch, and each wax station must re-sync to the current
epoch before it may operate again. A station may be slow but never fails:
while it is slow it cannot sync or wax, but it can always speed back up and
resume, so no station is permanently lost. Cars start out unwaxed. A
non-slow station that is synced to the current epoch may apply the final
wax coat to an unwaxed car, which records the car in the wax log and
permanently removes it from the pool of unwaxed cars, so it can never be
waxed again.

The system model has these actions: Reconfigure (bump the global epoch,
staling all stations), Sync (a non-slow station catches up to the current
epoch), BecomeSlow (a station becomes temporarily slow), SpeedUp (a slow
station recovers), and Wax (a synced, non-slow station irreversibly waxes
an unwaxed car and removes it from the unwaxed pool).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every car that has been given its final wax coat is no
longer in the unwaxed pool, so the irreversible wax step can never be
applied to the same car twice.

ring of wash stations and a central reservoir. Exclusive access to move

station currently holding the token may draw water from the reservoir into

never created or lost -- it only moves between the reservoir and the
station tanks -- so the grand total is constant. The token may be passed
to any other live station. A station other than the current token holder
may crash silently and stop participating; the token holder never crashes
while holding the token, so the token is never stranded, and a crashed
station may later recover.

live station), Draw (the token holder pulls one unit of water from the
reservoir into its tank), Return (the token holder pushes one unit from
its tank back to the reservoir), Crash (a non-holder station fails
silently), and Recover (a crashed station returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total water held across all station tanks plus the
water in the reservoir always equals the fixed amount in the system, so no
water is ever created or destroyed.

    /\ acked = {}

ReadRecord(c) ==
    /\ staged[c] = NoU
    /\ \E u \in Updates \ applied :
        /\ readSnap' = [readSnap EXCEPT ![c] = ver]
        /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = u]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, applied, acked, capacity>>

CommitApply(c) ==
    /\ staged[c] # NoU
    /\ readSnap[c] = ver
    /\ applied' = applied \cup {staged[c]}
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = NoU]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readSnap, acked, capacity>>

    /\ staged[c] # NoU
    /\ readSnap[c] # ver
    /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![c] = NoU]

    /\ u \notin acked
    /\ acked' = acked \cup {u}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, readSnap, staged, applied, capacity>>

    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, readSnap, staged, applied, acked>>

    Updates = {u1, u2}

    MaxCap = 3
    NoU = NoU

INVARIANT NoAckedUpdateLost
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network keeps a shared configuration record that
several client apps update using optimistic locking with retry. The record
carries a version number. To make a change a client first reads the record
(snapshotting the current version) and stages the update it intends to
apply, choosing an update that is not already applied. To commit, the
client re-checks that the version has not moved since its snapshot; only
on a matching version does the update get applied to the record and the
version bumped. If the version moved under it, the snapshot is stale and
the client abandons and retries, so a stale write can never silently
clobber a concurrent one. Once an update has actually been applied it may
be acknowledged back to its client. The number of enrolled devices is the
network's capacity and changes at runtime as devices are enrolled and
unenrolled.

version and stages an unapplied update), CommitApply (a client with a
fresh snapshot applies its staged update and bumps the version), RetryStale
(a client drops a staged update whose snapshot went stale), Ack
(acknowledge an already-applied update to its client), Enroll and Unenroll
(the device capacity changes at runtime).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every update that has been acknowledged to a client has
actually been applied to the shared record, so no acknowledged update is
ever lost.

    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, workerEpoch>>

    Printers = {p1, p2}
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    TotalJobs = 3
    MaxEpoch = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT JobsConserved
nl:
A print-shop job spooler holds a fixed batch of print jobs and moves them
between a central spool and individual printer queues. It uses
epoch-numbered reconfiguration: reconfiguring the spooler bumps the global
epoch, and each worker must re-sync to the current epoch before it may
move jobs. Jobs are never created or lost -- they only move between the
spool and the printer queues -- so the grand total is constant. A worker
synced to the current epoch may dispatch a job from the spool onto a
printer's queue, or recall a job from a printer's queue back to the spool.

printer queue to another, bypassing both the spool and the epoch check.

The system model has these actions: Reconfigure (bump the global epoch,
staling all workers), Sync (a stale worker catches up to the current
epoch), Dispatch (a current-epoch worker moves a spooled job onto a
printer queue), Recall (a current-epoch worker moves a queued job back to
the spool), and AdminShift (the admin override moves a job directly from
one printer queue to another).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of jobs waiting in the spool plus the number
queued across all printers always equals the fixed batch size, so no print
job is ever created or destroyed.

CONSTANTS Slots, Patrons, Free

    /\ available = Slots
    /\ online = Slots
    /\ waiting = {}

Request(pt) ==
    /\ pt \notin waiting
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {pt}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, available, online>>

Reserve(pt, s) ==
    /\ pt \in waiting
    /\ s \in online
    /\ s \in available
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = pt]
    /\ available' = available \ {s}
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {pt}
    /\ UNCHANGED online

Release(s) ==
    /\ holder[s] # Free
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ available' = IF s \in online THEN available \cup {s} ELSE available
    /\ UNCHANGED <<online, waiting>>

BringOnline(s) ==
    /\ s \notin online
    /\ online' = online \cup {s}
    /\ available' = IF holder[s] = Free THEN available \cup {s} ELSE available
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, waiting>>

    /\ s \in online
    /\ holder[s] = Free
    /\ online' = online \ {s}
    /\ available' = available \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, waiting>>

nl:
A library book reservation system hands out reservation slots to patrons,
guarding each slot with a compare-and-swap register that records either
the patron holding the slot or a Free marker. A slot can be reserved only
by atomically compare-and-swapping it from available to held, which
removes it from the available pool in the same step, so two patrons can
never both grab the same slot. A patron first requests service, then
reserves an online, available slot, which stamps the register with the
patron and clears the slot's available bit. Releasing a slot resets its
register to Free and, if the slot is still online, returns it to the
available pool. The number of online slots is the system's capacity and
changes at runtime: a slot can be brought online (becoming available if
its register is Free) or, if currently free, taken offline (removing it
from the available pool).

The system model has these actions: Request (a patron asks for a slot),
Reserve (a waiting patron compare-and-swaps an online, available slot to
held and clears its available bit), Release (a held slot's register is
reset to Free and it rejoins the available pool if online), BringOnline
(a slot enters service and becomes available when free), and TakeOffline
(a free slot leaves service, changing capacity at runtime).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any slot whose register shows it is held by a patron is
never simultaneously in the available pool, so no slot is ever double
allocated to two patrons.

    /\ c \notin approvals

    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, proposal, approvals>>

    /\ crashed' = crashed \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, proposal, approvals>>

INVARIANT TrainsConserved
nl:
A subway signalling block system moves a fixed number of trains between
track blocks under quorum control. Every proposed train movement must be
ratified by a quorum of signal controllers before it takes effect. Trains
are never created or lost; a movement only relocates one train from one
block to an adjacent block, so the grand total of trains is constant. A
movement is proposed between an occupied source block and a destination
block, which opens a fresh tally of approvals. Each live controller may
approve the pending proposal. Once a quorum of approvals is reached and
the source block is still occupied, the move commits: one train leaves the
source and arrives at the destination. A pending proposal may instead be
cancelled. Any controller may crash silently and stop approving, which
only makes quorums harder to reach; a crashed controller may recover.

The system model has these actions: Propose (open a movement from an
occupied source to a destination), Approve (a live controller ratifies the
pending move), CommitMove (relocate one train once a quorum approves),
CancelMove (drop the pending proposal), Crash (a controller fails
silently), and Recover (a crashed controller returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of trains summed across all track blocks
always equals the fixed fleet size, so no train is ever created or
destroyed.

instances that share one common pool of dispensing capacity. Each instance
independently runs leader election with failover to choose the node that
drives it. The two instances draw concurrent dispenses from the same

across both instances must never exceed that budget. A leader may begin a
dispense for its instance only while the combined number of in-progress
dispenses across both instances is still below the shared capacity; a
dispense later completes, freeing a unit of capacity. Any node may fail,
which vacates whichever instance leaderships it held and triggers
failover; a failed node may be restored.

installs a leader), Dispense (a live leader starts a dispense for its

A warehouse robot fleet updates a single shared inventory record, and
uses a token ring to grant exclusive write access so that concurrent
updates cannot clobber one another. Exactly one robot holds the token.
Updating the record is a read-modify-write: the token holder first reads
the current record value into its private buffer, then later writes back a
new value derived from what it read. Only the token holder is ever allowed
to have a read-modify-write in flight, which serializes updates and
guarantees no update is lost by being overwritten by a stale concurrent
write. The token may be passed to another live robot, but only when the
current holder has no read-modify-write in flight, so a half-finished
update is never abandoned to another robot. A robot other than the current
holder may crash silently, and a crashed robot may later recover.

The system model has these actions: PassToken (hand the token to another
live robot, only when no update is in flight), ReadModify (the holder
snapshots the record to begin an update), WriteBack (the holder writes the
derived new value and finishes the update), Crash (a non-holder robot
fails silently), and Recover (a crashed robot returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Only the current token holder can ever have a
read-modify-write update in flight, so two robots never update the shared
record concurrently and no update is ever lost.

    Players = {p1, p2}
    MaxVer = 2
    Free = Free

INVARIANT MatchLockMutex
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker protects a single critical
matchmaking resource (the ranked-match slot) with an optimistic lock. The
lock carries a version number and an owner field that is either Free or a
player. Acquiring is optimistic with retry: a player first reads the
lock's version into a private snapshot, then attempts to acquire only if
the lock is still Free and its snapshot still matches the current version;
a successful acquire compare-and-swaps the owner to that player, bumps the
version, and puts the player into the critical section. If the version
moved under it, the snapshot is stale and the player retries. Releasing
frees the owner, bumps the version, and removes the player from the
critical section. A player may be slow but never fails: while slow it
cannot read or acquire, but it can always speed back up, so it is only
delayed, never lost.

The system model has these actions: ReadLock (a non-slow player snapshots
the lock version), TryAcquire (a non-slow player with a fresh snapshot
compare-and-swaps a Free lock and enters the critical section), RetryStale
(a player drops a stale snapshot), Release (the holder leaves the critical
section and frees the lock), BecomeSlow (a player becomes temporarily
slow), and SpeedUp (a slow player recovers).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one player is ever inside the critical
matchmaking section at a time, so two distinct players never hold the
ranked-match slot simultaneously.

credential immediately becomes stale. Lease-grant messages can be
reordered in the network: a controller may receive the current grant (its
cached credential set to the current generation) or, because an older
grant message arrives late, receive a stale credential carrying an older
generation number. A controller may perform a load-shed action only when
it is the current holder and its cached credential matches the current
lease generation, so a controller whose lease expired or was superseded
(holding a stale, older-generation credential) and any controller that was
never the holder are locked out.

The system model has these actions: Tick (advance the clock), GrantLease
(bump the generation and install a holder with a fresh deadline),
ExpireLease (expire a past-deadline lease, bumping the generation and
vacating the holder), DeliverCurrent (the current holder caches the
current generation), DeliverStale (a reordered old grant caches an
older-generation credential), and Shed (the current holder with a matching
current credential performs a load shed).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A controller's cached credential equals the current lease
generation only when that controller is the current lease holder, so no
stale (expired or superseded) or never-authorized controller can pass the
credential check to shed load.
